newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: ISCOR BUOYED AHEAD OF FUTURES CLOSE-OUT.
newsitem.headline: ISCOR BUOYED AHEAD OF FUTURES CLOSE-OUT.

text.p: Iscor on Thursday was boosted by equity futures trade and a perception that lately it had been oversold and should start improving, dealers said.

Steel producer Iscor is weighted on the industrial and the all-share index, making it an easy tool for futures players to use to manipulate the spot market ahead of the futures close-out on September 16, dealers said.
"Iscor is up on the fact that the futures guys are in the market and it has been oversold in the last six months," one dealer told Reuters.
Iscor reached a high of 295 cents, adding 5.4 percent to its market value, in intraday trade before settling at 293 cents, 13 cents higher after 1.5 million shares traded valued at 4.3 million rand.
"It is the biggest rise we have seen in Iscor in a long time. Hopefully it indicates a change in the steel industry," another dealer said.
Iscor posted poor results for the year ended June of 35.7 cents per share versus 36.4 cents.
It warned that results for the first half to December 1996 would be weak as it saw no immediate prospect of the domestic steel market improving.
